claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
The relatively low hardness and strength are governed by localized shear-band formation and associated microstructural evolution during deformation.
In-situ TEM or XRD combined with molecular-dynamics simulations can reveal the proposed deformation mechanism.
The initial material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state.
The proposed intervention is compressive loading.
The hypothesis is intended to apply at temperatures up to 600 °C.
Compressive deformation produces localized shear bands and associated microstructural evolution.
Deformation-induced microstructural changes, including shear bands, affect alloy hardness and strength.
Localized shear bands and associated microstructural evolution decrease hardness and strength relative to other high-entropy alloys.
CoCrFeNiTi retains favorable plasticity and machinability despite its lower hardness and strength.
The proposed baseline is the hardness and strength of the same simple-solid-solution alloy without deformation.
Failure to observe localized shear bands during deformation would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to find a correlation between microstructural evolution and decreased hardness and strength would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is the undeformed starting alloy, but the predicted outcome is framed relative to other high-entropy alloys rather than relative to that baseline, so the proposed comparison is internally inconsistent.

The low hardness and strength of the initial simple-solid-solution state are attributed to deformation-induced shear bands, while the stated baseline is explicitly without deformation; the hypothesis does not explain how a deformation-induced structure governs the pre-deformation properties.
